files.Title: ParquetNeo.BatchRead
files.Summary: The outcome of a batch read.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.BloomFilterSettings
files.Summary: A bloom filter for a column, see .

files.Title: ParquetNeo.ColumnOrder
files.Summary: Order of a column's type-defined sort (thrift ColumnOrder union).

files.Title: ParquetNeo.ColumnReader
files.Summary: Reads the values of one column chunk, a batch at a time. Obtain it from and dispose it when done, which returns its buffers to the pool.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.ColumnSettingKinds
files.Summary: The kinds of ColumnSettings a column type can take.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.ColumnTypes.ColumnSettings
files.Summary: What can be adjusted about the column a type is written to. A type takes the settings that suit it (see ) and ignores the others.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.ColumnTypes.ColumnType<TValue>
files.Summary: Everything about storing one .NET type in a Parquet column: the column it gets by default, which columns of a file it can be read from or written to, and how a batch of values is converted to and from the physical type and passed to the column reader or writer. The built-in types are found with ; an own type derives from this class.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.ColumnTypes.ColumnType
files.Summary: What every column type says without knowing its .NET type: which one it is, the column it creates, and whether a column fits it. Derive from , which adds reading and writing, to add a type of your own.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.ColumnTypes.ColumnTypeRegistry
files.Summary: Finds the that reads and writes values of a .NET type: the built-in ones, any enum (as the name of its value), and the ones added with . The serializer uses it to decide how a property is stored, so registering a column type teaches it a new type for its properties.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.ColumnWriter
files.Summary: Writes the values of one column of a row group. Obtain it from , call one of the Write… methods one or more times, then move on to the next column.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Compression.BrotliCodec
files.Summary: Brotli (RFC 7932), via the span-based and .

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Compression.CodecRegistry
files.Summary: The codecs available to readers and writers. A new registry holds the built-in ones (uncompressed, Gzip, Brotli); codecs from add-on packages (ParquetNeo.Compression.Snappy, .Zstd and .Lz4) are registered explicitly.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Compression.GzipCodec
files.Summary: GZIP (RFC 1952), via . Decompression accepts several members back to back, as the spec asks of readers.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Compression.ICodec
files.Summary: A page compression codec. Parquet stores the uncompressed and compressed size of every page, so both directions work on buffers of known size and never need to grow or stream.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Compression.Lz4.Lz4RawCodec
files.Summary: LZ4_RAW: the plain LZ4 block format, using the managed K4os.Compression.LZ4 library. This is not the deprecated, Hadoop-framed LZ4 codec. Register it with CodecRegistry.Default.AddLz4Raw().

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Compression.Snappy.SnappyCodec
files.Summary: Snappy in its raw block format (no framing), which is what Parquet pages use, using the managed Snappier library. Register it with CodecRegistry.Default.AddSnappy().

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Compression.UncompressedCodec
files.Summary: The "no compression" codec: data is copied as it is.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Compression.Zstd.ZstdCodec
files.Summary: ZSTD (RFC 8878) using the managed ZstdSharp.Port library. Register it with CodecRegistry.Default.AddZstd().

files.Title: ParquetNeo.ConvertedType
files.Summary: Legacy type annotations, superseded by LogicalType.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Data.ParquetDataReader
files.Summary: Reads a Parquet file as a , so that it can go wherever a query result can: SqlBulkCopy, , Dapper and the like.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Data.ParquetDataReaderOptions
files.Summary: Settings for .

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Data.ParquetDataWriter
files.Summary: Writes the rows of an (a database query, a through , or any other reader) as a Parquet file. Each column of the reader becomes a column of the file, typed by : the types of , which are the ones ParquetSerializer writes. A column is optional unless the reader's schema table says AllowDBNull is false, and a decimal takes the precision and scale the schema table gives (38 and 18 otherwise).

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Data.ParquetDataWriterOptions
files.Summary: Settings for .

files.Title: ParquetNeo.DataModel.ParquetColumnAttribute
files.Summary: Names the column a property is written to, or its position among the columns. Without it the column has the property's name.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.DataModel.ParquetDecimalAttribute
files.Summary: The precision and scale of a property's column. Without it a decimal is written with a precision of 38 and a scale of 18. A value with more decimals than the scale, or more digits than the precision, cannot be written. The column is INT32 up to a precision of 9, INT64 up to 18, and a fixed-length byte array above that.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.DataModel.ParquetDictionaryAttribute
files.Summary: How the column of a property is dictionary encoded (every column of a collection or dictionary, but not of the properties of an object inside it, which have their own attributes), instead of . A dictionary stores each distinct value once and the rows refer to it, which pays off when values repeat and is wasted work when they do not.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.DataModel.ParquetEncodingAttribute
files.Summary: The encoding of the values of a property's column (every column of a collection or dictionary, but not of the properties of an object inside it, which have their own attributes), instead of PLAIN; see for what suits which data. An encoding the column's type cannot use is an when serializing. Encodings set in the options win over this one.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.DataModel.ParquetIgnoreAttribute
files.Summary: Leaves a property out of the file.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.DataModel.ParquetSerializableAttribute
files.Summary: Asks the source generator for the mapping of a type, so that the serializer never looks at the type by reflection: it works with trimming and Native AOT, and does not compile code when it is first used. Put it on the type, or, for a type you do not own, on the assembly: [assembly: ParquetSerializable(typeof(TheirType))]. The mapping is registered when the assembly is loaded, so is used as before. A type without it keeps working by reflection, which is not safe with trimming or Native AOT.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.DataModel.ParquetTimeAttribute
files.Summary: The unit and meaning of the column of a property. Without it times are written in microseconds, as wall-clock readings.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.DataModel.ParquetTimestampAttribute
files.Summary: The unit and meaning of the column of a or property. Without it timestamps are written in microseconds, as moments in UTC.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.DataPageVersion
files.Summary: The layout of the data pages a writer produces.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.DictionaryMode
files.Summary: How a column is dictionary encoded; see DictionarySettings and ParquetWriterOptions.ColumnDictionaries.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.DictionarySettings
files.Summary: How one column is dictionary encoded; see .

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Exceptions.CompressionException
files.Summary: Thrown when the compressed data of a page is invalid, or does not decompress to the size its page header declares.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Exceptions.CorruptColumnException
files.Summary: Thrown when the pages of a column chunk contradict each other or the metadata: counts that do not add up, dictionary or level problems, or an encoding the column's type cannot use.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Exceptions.EncodingException
files.Summary: Thrown when encoded values or levels cannot be decoded: the data is too short, or is not valid for its encoding (PLAIN, RLE, delta, byte-stream-split).

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Exceptions.InvalidSchemaException
files.Summary: Thrown when the schema of a file is not a well-formed tree of groups and columns.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Exceptions.MetadataException
files.Summary: Thrown when metadata cannot be decoded: the Thrift data of the footer or of a page header is malformed, or recorded statistics have the wrong size.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Exceptions.ParquetException
files.Summary: The base of the exceptions this library throws for a file it cannot read, so that one catch handles them all. Misuse of the API itself is reported with the standard exceptions instead, such as and .

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Exceptions.ParquetFormatException
files.Summary: Thrown when the layout of a Parquet file is wrong: it is truncated, lacks the PAR1 markers, or its footer and row groups do not fit in it.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Exceptions.SchemaMismatchException
files.Summary: Thrown when the schema of a file does not fit the type it is read into: a column that is missing, or stored as a type the property cannot hold.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Exceptions.ValueConversionException
files.Summary: Thrown when a stored value is valid Parquet but cannot be represented by the .NET type it is read as, such as a date before year 1 or a time beyond a day.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.FilterColumn
files.Summary: A column a condition is put on; see .

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Linq.ParquetDataset<T>
files.Summary: The rows of a file or of the files of a directory, as an ; see .

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Linq.ParquetDataset
files.Summary: Opens datasets: files of rows of one type, to be queried with LINQ.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Linq.ParquetDatasetOptions
files.Summary: Settings for a .

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Linq.ParquetQueryPlan
files.Summary: What a query reads of a dataset, from the footers of its files; see .

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Linq.ParquetQueryableExtensions
files.Summary: Operations on the queries of a that LINQ does not have.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.ListStyle
files.Summary: How a list is laid out in the schema. Writers have used several; readers must accept them all.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.LogicalTypeKind
files.Summary: Kind of a LogicalType. Values are the field ids of the thrift union.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Metadata.ColumnChunk
files.Summary: Location and metadata of one column chunk (thrift ColumnChunk). Encryption fields are skipped.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Metadata.ColumnIndex
files.Summary: The smallest and largest value of every data page of a column chunk, and how many are null (thrift ColumnIndex); entry i of each list is for the page at i in the . The bounds are encoded as the statistics of the column are.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Metadata.ColumnMetaData
files.Summary: Metadata of one column chunk (thrift ColumnMetaData). Geospatial statistics are not read yet.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Metadata.FileMetaData
files.Summary: The Parquet footer (thrift FileMetaData). Unknown fields, including the extension field 32767, are skipped when reading; encryption fields are not supported yet.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Metadata.Headers.BloomFilterHeader
files.Summary: The header in front of the bits of a bloom filter (thrift BloomFilterHeader). The only filter the format defines is split block, hashed with xxHash64 and not compressed.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Metadata.Headers.PageHeader
files.Summary: Header preceding every page in a column chunk (thrift PageHeader).

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Metadata.LogicalType
files.Summary: A logical type annotation (thrift LogicalType union). Only the parameters relevant to are meaningful.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Metadata.OffsetIndex
files.Summary: The positions of the data pages of a column chunk (thrift OffsetIndex), so that a reader can go to a page without reading the ones before it.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Metadata.PageEncodingStats
files.Summary: How many pages of a type used an encoding (thrift PageEncodingStats).

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Metadata.PageLocation
files.Summary: Where a data page of a column chunk is, and which row it starts with (thrift PageLocation).

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Metadata.SchemaElement
files.Summary: One node of the flattened, depth-first schema tree (thrift SchemaElement).

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Metadata.SizeStatistics
files.Summary: Size statistics of a column chunk (thrift SizeStatistics).

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Metadata.SortingColumn
files.Summary: A column a row group is sorted by (thrift SortingColumn).

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Metadata.Statistics
files.Summary: Column statistics for a page or column chunk (thrift Statistics).

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Nested.ColumnStructure
files.Summary: The shape of the data in one column, as validity and offsets instead of definition and repetition levels: for each optional node on the way to the column whether its value is present, and for each repeated node where each list starts and ends. It is the columnar form of nested data (the same idea as the validity and offsets of an Arrow array), and it converts both ways with the levels the reader returns and the writer takes.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Nested.ListLayout
files.Summary: Where the parts of a list are in the schema; see .

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Nested.MapLayout
files.Summary: Where the parts of a map are in the schema; see .

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Nested.NestedSchema
files.Summary: Builds the standard LIST and MAP layouts and recognizes the layouts found in files, including the legacy ones.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Nested.StructureLevel
files.Summary: The structure one optional or repeated schema node adds to a column: validity for an optional node, offsets for a repeated one. Create it with or .

files.Title: ParquetNeo.ParquetEncoding
files.Summary: Value encodings (thrift Encoding).

files.Title: ParquetNeo.ParquetFileReader
files.Summary: Reads a Parquet file one row group and one leaf column at a time, with the definition and repetition levels of nested columns. The stream must be readable and seekable, because the metadata sits at the end of the file.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.ParquetFileWriter
files.Summary: Writes a Parquet file, one row group at a time. Columns are written one leaf column at a time, with the definition and repetition levels for nested ones. The stream only needs to be writable: offsets are counted rather than read from the stream, so it need not be seekable.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.ParquetFilter
files.Summary: A condition on the values of columns, which a reader checks against the statistics of each row group (the smallest and largest value, and how many are null) to skip the row groups that cannot hold a row that satisfies it. Build one with and combine with , and .

files.Title: ParquetNeo.ParquetReaderOptions
files.Summary: Settings for a . The limits protect against corrupt or hostile files.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.ParquetWriterOptions
files.Summary: Settings for a .

files.Title: ParquetNeo.PhysicalType
files.Summary: Physical (storage) type of a column (thrift Type).

files.Title: ParquetNeo.RowGroupReader
files.Summary: Gives access to the columns of one row group.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.RowGroupWriter
files.Summary: Writes one row group: every column of the schema, in schema order, each with the same number of rows. Create it with , call once per column, and dispose it (or call ) to finish the group.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.RowRange
files.Summary: A run of rows of a row group: the position of the first and how many.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.RowSelection
files.Summary: Some rows of a row group, as ascending runs that do not touch. Given to so that the column is read for only those rows; the pages that hold none of them are not read. Rows count from the first of the group, and a row of a repeated column is a whole record (a list), however many values it has.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Schema.GroupNode
files.Summary: An inner node holding other nodes (a struct, or part of a list or map).

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Schema.ParquetSchema
files.Summary: The schema of a Parquet file as a tree, with the definition and repetition levels of every node and the leaf in the order their chunks are stored.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Schema.PrimitiveNode
files.Summary: A leaf of the schema: one stored column.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Schema.SchemaNode
files.Summary: A node of the schema tree: either a or a column.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Serialization.Generated.AssembleRow<TRow>
files.Summary: Creates a row from the values of the columns, which is what the source generator writes for each type.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Serialization.Generated.MappingRegistry
files.Summary: Where the source generator registers the mapping of each type marked , when the assembly is loaded. The mapping is made the first time the serializer needs it. Not for use in code you write yourself.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Serialization.Generated.ReadMapping<TRow>
files.Summary: How rows of a type are read, made by a .

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Serialization.Generated.ReadMappingBuilder<TRow>
files.Summary: Describes how a row type is read from columns, and gets the code that creates each object from their values. What the source generator writes for a type uses it, and nothing at run time looks at the type: no reflection, and no code is compiled. Not for use in code you write yourself.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Serialization.Generated.RowSink
files.Summary: Where the code written by the source generator puts the values of an object: a property that is a column of its own goes to the column with its number, counted from the first column of the object, and a property that is an object, a collection or a dictionary goes to its place among the properties, counted from zero. Not for use in code you write yourself.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Serialization.Generated.RowSource
files.Summary: Where the code written by the source generator takes the values of an object from: a property that is a column of its own is read from the column with its number, counted from the first column of the object, and a property that is an object, a collection or a dictionary from its place among the properties, counted from zero. Not for use in code you write yourself.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Serialization.Generated.ShredRow<TRow>
files.Summary: Gives the values of a row to the columns, which is what the source generator writes for each type.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Serialization.Generated.WriteMapping<TRow>
files.Summary: How rows of a type are written, made by a .

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Serialization.Generated.WriteMappingBuilder<TRow>
files.Summary: Describes how a row type is written as columns, and gets the code that gives the values of each object to them. What the source generator writes for a type uses it, and nothing at run time looks at the type: no reflection, and no code is compiled. Not for use in code you write yourself.

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Serialization.ParquetDeserializerOptions
files.Summary: Settings for reading rows with .

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Serialization.ParquetSerializer
files.Summary: Writes objects as rows of a Parquet file ( and ), and reads rows back (, and their asynchronous forms; see the remarks below for what reading supports). Each public property becomes a column, named after the property and typed by the convention below, which attributes on the property adjust: , , , , and .

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Serialization.ParquetSerializerOptions
files.Summary: Settings for .

files.Title: ParquetNeo.Statistics.ColumnStatistics
files.Summary: The statistics of one column chunk, decoded to .NET values. Obtain it from .

files.Title: ParquetNeo.StructureLevelKind
files.Summary: What a StructureLevel records about its schema node.
